10 استجّم , as an intrans. verb: see 1, in five places. ―
-b2- It is said in a trad., مَنْ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَسْتَجِمَّ لَهُ النَّاسُ قِيَامًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ, i. e. [Whoso loveth that men] should collect themselves to him, standing in his presence, and confining themselves to him, [let him take his sitting-place in the fire of Hell:] or, accord. as some relate it, يستخمّ; see art. خم; (TA;) and, as some, يَسْتَخِيمَ. (TA in art. خيم, q. v.) ―
-b3- استجمّت الأَرْضُ The land put forth its plants, or herbage, (K, TA,) so that it became like the [hair termed] جمّة [i. e. جُمَّة]. (TA.) ＝
-A2- As a trans. verb: see 1, near the end of the paragraph, in two
places: ―
-b2- and see 4. ―
-b3- اُسْتُجِمَّتْ جَمَّةُ المَآءِ [The supply of water that had collected after drawing] was drunk. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
